evidence: Ov. Met. 6.349: ūsus commūnis aquārum est
terms.comment: The opposite is proprius, one’s own (Quint. 7.3.24, Lewis & Short). The general good is commūnis ūtilitās (Gell. 12.1.24).

terms.gloss: of all together, of the whole
evidence: Cic. Off. 3.26: ūtilitās ūnīus cujusque et ūniversōrum
Liv. 22.32.2: ūniversa dīmicātiō, a general engagement (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: All taken together, as against each one (singulī).

terms.gloss: general (as against particular); of a kind
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.96: generāle quoddam decōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A word of philosophy and rhetoric, opposed to speciālis; rare before Augustus, frequent in Quintilian and Seneca (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quid prohibētis aquīs? ūsus commūnis aquārum est. nec sōlem proprium nātūra nec āëra fēcit nec tenuēs undās: ad pūblica mūnera vēnī
phrases.english: Why keep me from the water? Water is for everyone to use. Nature made neither the sun nor the air nor the clear water anyone’s own: I have come to gifts that belong to all.

phrases.latin: Ergō ūnum dēbet esse omnibus prōpositum, ut eadem sit ūtilitās ūnīus cujusque et ūniversōrum
phrases.english: So everyone should have one aim: that the good of each and the good of all should be the same

phrases.latin: vetus verbum hoc quidem est: commūnia esse amīcōrum inter sē omnia
phrases.english: it is an old saying, this: friends have everything in common
